rationale_evidence.anchor: KnowledgeOS cannot yet be declared a lattice: Join may not exist under a consistency requirement
rationale_evidence.statement: Notes a lattice requires every pair K_A,K_B to have Meet(K_A,K_B) and Join(K_A,K_B), which 'we cannot yet claim'. Example: K_A={p}, K_B={not-p} give a candidate join {p,not-p} under set inclusion, but if a knowledge state requires consistency the union is not admissible, so Join may not exist within the consistent subset -- 'KnowledgeOS cannot yet be declared a lattice. This is exactly the kind of mathematical restraint we want.'

- [S0956] types=[FORMALIZATION, PRINCIPLE] scope=OBJECT — "When E1,E2|=p and E3|=not-p, KnowledgeOS must preserve the competing evidence for p and not-p. - [S0956] types=[DISTINCTION, DEFINITION] scope=OBJECT — "Distinguishes Ignorance (Evidence(p)=empty, leading to Unknown(p)) from Uncertainty (information exists but does not strongly determine the proposition, e.g. P(p)=0.65, so Unknown != Uncertain) from Contradiction (evidence supports competing propositions, P(supports p)>0 and P(supports not-p)>0, so Contradiction != Uncertainty). - [S0956] types=[FORMALIZATION, WARNING] scope=OBJECT — "Represents K(p) = (Support+(p), Support-(p), Uncertainty, Provenance), arguing a single scalar confidence cannot cleanly distinguish strong asymmetrical support (Support+=0.8, Support-=0.1) from strong disagreement (Support+=0.8, Support-=0.8). Warns S+, S- in [0,1] must not automatically be interpreted as P(p) and P(not-p) -- they become probabilities only if statistical semantics justify it; if a probabilistic model P(p|E) is explicitly defined, P(not-p|E)=1-P(p|E) for a binary exhaustive proposition, but generic support scores need not obey that equation. Separates an Epistemic layer (Support, Conflict, Provenance) from a Statistical layer (Probability, Likelihood, Posterior) that interact but are not identical." (anchor: "Two-dimensional epistemic state K(p)=(Support+,Support-,Uncertainty,Provenance); not automatically probabilities")

Experiment 3: K_A={p}, K_B={not-p} merge to K_M={p,not-p} yielding Conflict(p) -- PASS. Experiment 4: attempting Resolve(K_M,p) without additional evidence or policy is Rejected -- PASS. - [S0956] types=[FORMALIZATION, EXAMPLE] scope=OBJECT — "Experiment: K_A has p-version-1, K_B has p-version-2; a naive union produces both, but p_2 may semantically supersede p_1, requiring a version-aware Merge_v(K_A,K_B) that retains both historical states while defining Active(p)=p_2 -- not ordinary set union. Experiment: p valid during [0,10] and not-p valid during [10,20] do not conflict since the intervals do not overlap, so contradiction must be temporal: Conflict(p) is required only when competing claims overlap in the relevant semantic scope -- Conflict(p,t), with TemporalScope as part of epistemic reasoning." (anchor: "Version-aware merge for supersession; temporal-scope-bounded contradiction Conflict(p,t)")
- [S0956] types=[DISTINCTION, PRINCIPLE] scope=OBJECT — "Experiment: p_A ('SystemA is Healthy') and p_B ('SystemB is Unhealthy') are not contradictory despite superficial similarity -- a naive string comparison could incorrectly infer conflict, so PropositionEquality must consider Subject, Predicate, Object, Scope, and potentially Time. Notes semantically equivalent but syntactically different propositions ('SystemA is healthy' vs 'SystemA hasStatus Healthy') require explicit SemanticMapping, never assumed string equality -- giving ClaimIdentity != TextIdentity, essential for AI-generated knowledge. Experiment: two agents' differently-phrased claims may remain Unknown as to equivalence unless the semantic-normalization mapping is sufficiently reliable -- PASS, restated as another epistemic firewall instance: AI semantic similarity must not automatically become Identity; similarity is evidence for equivalence, not equivalence itself." (anchor: "Typed proposition identity prevents naive scope conflation; ClaimIdentity != TextIdentity; semantic similarity is another epistemic firewall instance")
- [S0956] types=[FORMALIZATION, DISTINCTION] scope=OBJECT — "Defines a rigorous merge pipeline: K_A,K_B -> CandidateAlignment -> SemanticValidation -> Merge -> ConflictDetection -> Resolution if applicable -- contrasted with RAG, which generally just combines retrieved text; KnowledgeOS instead combines StructuredPropositions + Evidence + Semantics + TemporalScope." (anchor: "Five-stage knowledge-merge pipeline; contrast with RAG's plain-text combination")
- [S0956] types=[FORMALIZATION, EXAMPLE] scope=OBJECT — "Worked example: prior P(p)=0.5 (odds O(p)=1), evidence E with likelihood ratio LR=P(E|p)/P(E|not-p)=4, posterior odds O(p|E)=O(p)*LR=4, posterior P(p|E)=4/(1+4)=0.8. Explicitly warns P(p|E)=0.8 means only that, under the specified probabilistic model -- it does not mean Truth(p)=0.8 and does not automatically mean Confidence=0.8. If the domain supports Bayesian inference as a first-class operation UpdateBelief(P,E)->P', the result should record Prior, Evidence, LikelihoodModel, Posterior, ModelVersion, giving Bayesian provenance P -> E -> LikelihoodModel -> P' consistent with the general provenance architecture." (anchor: "Full Bayesian-update worked example via likelihood ratios; posterior != truth, != confidence")
- [S0956] types=[EXAMPLE, WARNING] scope=OBJECT — "Worked example: P(p)=0.5, E1 gives LR1=4 (P(p|E1)=0.8), E2 gives LR2=0.25, combined LR=4*0.25=1, so P(p|E1,E2)=0.5 -- illustrating conflicting evidence returning the posterior toward the prior without discarding either evidence -- PASS. Warns the multiplication LR1*LR2 assumes appropriate conditional independence, which must be recorded, not blindly assumed; if E1 and E2 share an underlying source, treating them as independent overstates evidence (EvidenceDependency). States the major statistical requirement EvidenceCount != EvidenceStrength: 'ten copies of the same report are not necessarily ten independent pieces of evidence'. Experiment: E1=E2=E, naive multiplication would incorrectly give LR^2, but the provenance/dependency model identifies E1≡E2 so evidence is not double-counted -- PASS given available dependency identity, distinguishing MoreDocuments from MoreIndependentEvidence." (anchor: "Conflicting-evidence Bayesian example (LR returns to 1.0); evidence independence required; EvidenceCount != EvidenceStrength (duplicate-evidence non-double-counting)")
- [S0956] types=[FORMALIZATION] scope=OBJECT — "Consolidates the claim object as C=(P,E,S,T,U,V,M): Proposition, Evidence/provenance, epistemic Status, Temporal scope, Uncertainty, Version, semantic (M)eaning/context -- 'becoming the central knowledge object'. States a KnowledgeOS Claim is not merely a sentence but a structured epistemic object: Claim != Text. The complete knowledge state K={C1,...,Cn} plus relations R(K) and provenance Prov(K) forms a knowledge graph G_K=(C,R) with typed edges (Supports, Contradicts, DerivedFrom, Supersedes, Refines, DependsOn) -- noting not every relation is epistemic (e.g. Causes belongs to causal semantics), so the knowledge graph may contain typed relations from multiple contexts while ownership remains context-specific." (anchor: "Seven-field Claim=(P,E,S,T,U,V,M) object; Claim != Text; knowledge graph G_K=(C,R) with typed epistemic edges")
- [S0956] types=[RESTATEMENT, HYPOTHESIS] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "States the Step 60 central finding: KnowledgeOS knowledge is a versioned, provenance-aware, temporally-scoped, partially ordered collection of structured propositions -- 'a much stronger statement than KnowledgeOS stores knowledge'. Confirms the basic set-union representation has semilattice properties (commutative, associative, idempotent), but the full semantic merge (contradiction, temporal validity, supersession, semantic equivalence, probabilistic updates, provenance, policy) means KnowledgeOS cannot yet be asserted to be a semilattice; lattice structure remains an open hypothesis." (anchor: "Central finding: KnowledgeOS knowledge is a versioned, provenance-aware, temporally-scoped, partially ordered collection of structured propositions; lattice status left open")
- [S0956] types=[FORMALIZATION, DISTINCTION] scope=OBJECT — "Introduces the architecture's two fundamentally different state spaces: Operational state (wants controlled authoritative transitions: Decision/Action -> Authorization -> Execution -> Outcome) and Epistemic state (may legitimately branch, conflict, merge, and revise: Claims/Hypotheses -> Evidence/Support -> Conflict/Merge -> Revision/Learning), both feeding into Governance -- 'this distinction is extremely important' and 'a significant refinement'." (anchor: "Operational State vs Epistemic State architectural split")
- [S0956] types=[RESTATEMENT, OPEN-QUESTION, FUTURE-RESEARCH] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Declares STEP 60 -- PASS WITH A MATHEMATICAL QUALIFICATION: KnowledgeState, KnowledgeMerge, Conflict, Uncertainty, TemporalScope, Provenance, and BayesianUpdate were successfully derived without collapsing them into one concept, but lattice structure remains an open hypothesis. Opens Step 61 (Information Gain, Uncertainty and Epistemic Quality): can KnowledgeOS mathematically quantify what was learned (e.g. P(p): 0.5->0.8, was InformationGain>0, how much), accounting for correlated evidence and worsening calibration despite more extreme probability, with the central question of whether KnowledgeOS can distinguish 'more confident' from 'actually better informed' -- framed as crucial for KnowledgeOS to become 'the mathematical knowledge substrate for AI engineering, rather than simply another AI/RAG storage system'." (anchor: "Step 60 verdict PASS WITH A MATHEMATICAL QUALIFICATION; opens Step 61 on information gain, uncertainty and epistemic quality")
- [S0957] types=[FORMALIZATION, EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT] scope=OBJECT — "Defines Delta EQ = EQ(K_{t+1}) - EQ(K_t), noting this is not automatically a scalar since EQ is multidimensional; example where Uncertainty decreases but ProvenanceQuality decreases has no universal 'improved or not' answer -- 'EpistemicQuality is generally a partial order, not necessarily a single number... an important mathematical finding'. Gives a Pareto interpretation: K_B succ K_A only if K_B is at least as good in all relevant dimensions and strictly better in one; otherwise the states may be incomparable, illustrated by a four-dimension table (evidence strength, freshness, independence, uncertainty) where neither K_A nor K_B dominates, giving K_A parallel K_B. Experiment: attempting K_A>K_B with no dominance relation correctly yields Incomparable -- PASS, refining the earlier K_A⪯K_B hypothesis toward MoreInformative subject to Reliability/Independence/Freshness/Validity rather than MoreClaims=Better." (anchor: "Epistemic quality is generally a partial order, not a single number; Pareto incomparability among knowledge states")
- [S0970] types=[FORMALIZATION, EXPERIMENTAL-RESULT] scope=OBJECT — "Defines merge M(S_A,S_B): for independent artifacts M=S_A union S_B; for conflicting claims M=S_merged+Conflict (never OneWinner). Experiment 6: A and B independently producing contradictory claims yields a MergedState containing Claim_A, Claim_B, and a ConflictRecord -- PASS. Contrasts with Git-style text merging ('can these modifications coexist') versus KnowledgeOS's semantic question ('what is the epistemic relationship'). States merge must be a domain (bounded-context) operation, not one generic infrastructure function -- EvidenceContext and DecisionContext may have different merge semantics. Experiment 7: using one universal merge algorithm across evidence/claims/policies/authorizations yields ArchitecturalFailure -- explicitly FAIL, 'the semantics differ too much'." (anchor: "Epistemic merge as a domain-specific operation, never a generic infrastructure function (generic-merge experiment FAILs)")
